# OpenShell deciding check (2026-10-26)

**Question:** does a policy generated by Warrant from a warrant actually allow and block the right requests
inside a real NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox?

**Answer: yes.**

## Setup
- OpenShell 0.1.5 (`openshell_0.1.5-1_amd64.deb`, checksum verified by the official installer)
- Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL 2, native Docker Engine 29.1.3 (`docker.io`), compute driver `docker`
- Sandbox image: `deploy/sandbox.Dockerfile` (NVIDIA base image `nvcr.io/nvidia/base/ubuntu:24.04` plus curl)
- Warrant: one capability, `GET https://example.com/` only, rendered by `warrant.policy.render_policy`

## Results (requests made with curl from inside the sandbox)

| Request | Expected | Observed | OpenShell log |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET https://example.com/` | allowed | HTTP 200 | `HTTP:GET ALLOWED ... [policy:example_read_home engine:l7]` |
| `POST https://example.com/` | denied (method) | HTTP 403 | `HTTP:POST DENIED ... reason=POST / not permitted by policy` |
| `GET https://example.com/other` | denied (path) | HTTP 403 | `HTTP:GET DENIED ... reason=GET /other not permitted by policy` |
| `GET https://www.iana.org/` | denied (host) | no connection | `NET:REFUSE DENIED www.iana.org [reason:policy_dns_ineligible]` |

The raw decision log is kept in `tests/fixtures/openshell_0.1.5_ocsf.log` and parsed by
`warrant.enforce.openshell.parse_ocsf` in `tests/test_openshell.py`.

## Findings that changed the code
- `process.run_as_user: sandbox` fails on the default image (no such user). Warrant now leaves process and
  filesystem settings to OpenShell's defaults.
- Sandbox names are limited to 19 characters.
- Docker Desktop cannot be used as the engine on WSL: the supervisor runs with host networking and expects the
  gateway on 127.0.0.1, which is Docker Desktop's VM, not the WSL distro.
